w: During the darshan of Thakorji in the morning, Swamishri sprayed colored water on the murtis of Harikrishna Maharaj, Mukundanand Brahmachari, Gopinath Dev, etc. Swamishri also briefly sprayed colored water on sadhus and devotees.

This year because of the earthquake calamity, the pushpadolotsav was cancelled and only an assembly was held in the morning. In his blessings, Swamishri said, "Whatever talents we find in people have all been blessed by God... But when we acquire a talent we become arrogant. And God's talents are such that everyone experiences joy and happiness..." Then Swamishri and the assembly of sadhus and devotees offered peace prayers for the departed souls in the earthquake disaster and for the early rehabilitation of the homeless.
Swamishri then worshipped the murti of Lord Harikrishna Maharaj and sprayed a little colored water.

After Swamishri’s morning puja he gave parshad and bhagvati diksha to 42 youths. Kothari Swami placed the kanthi round each youth’s neck, Dr Swami draped a gatariyu, Mahant Swami placed a pagh and Swamishri gave the guru mantra and blessings. (For details see Swaminarayan Bliss, April 2010, inside back title.)

Today Pramukh Swami Maharaj was to give diksha to the sadhaks. On this occasion, when Swamishri came for darshan in Shastriji Maharaj's room, a sadhu sang, "Shyam piya mori rang de chunariya..." (Dark beloved, colour my veil...). This sadhu had a dark complexion. In this context he said, "The colour of my body is already fast, but bless me that my heart becomes saffron."
"The colour of the body may be whatever it is, there is no need for that. What is needed is devotion of the heart." Swamishri explained the glory of inner devotion.

Doing darshan, Pramukh Swami Maharaj came to the Rupchowki on top of the mandir. A crowd of sadhus had gathered here, those who had come from abroad and those from abroad who were staying at the training centre here. They all said, "To become a sadhu, learn saintliness and give up our natures."
Swamishri said, "Give up what?"
A sadhu said, "Our natures."
"Do you have any?" Swamishri asked.
The sadhu said, "Please be gracious."
Swamishri said, "I have been gracious already. How much more? I made you sadhus."
Saying this, and passing on, he said, "Everyone's natures will be shed."

Today thousands of devotees had gathered for the diksha (initiation) ceremony. Some volunteers had set out from Ahmedabad early in the morning to attend this occasion. Five volunteers from the Hirawadi area, among them assistant director Karsanbhai I. Patel, Nilkanthbhai D. Thumar, Ambarishbhai Nanjibhai Patel and Mukeshbhai Vasani, were coming to Sarangpur early in the morning when their car collided with a truck near Dhandhuka, and four of the volunteers passed away on the spot. The fifth volunteer, Ghanshyambhai Thumar, was seriously injured. Pramukh Swami Maharaj received the news while the diksha ceremony was going on, so he had the sadhus make all the arrangements.

Even on such a transcendental and divine occasion, Swamishri did not fail to pay tribute to them in his blessings. Speaking of this during his blessings, Swamishri said, "Today something has happened that makes us sad. Devotees were coming here by car and there was an accident near Dhandhuka, and four brothers passed away. They were coming here itself, they were directors, it has happened by Maharaj's wish. God is the doer. Whether to extend or end a life is all a matter of God's wish. If we have that knowledge, there is no wailing. Whatever God has done is good. So today let us do dhun for that event. Let us do a little dhun so that their souls find peace, God keeps them happy, and there is peace in their families too." Saying this, Swamishri himself began the dhun "Swaminarayan... Swaminarayan...". For about five minutes Swamishri himself led the dhun.

Today Swamishri was to give diksha to the sadhaks. On this occasion, when Swamishri came for darshan in Shastriji Maharaj's room, a sadhu sang, 'Shyam piya mori rang de chunariya...' (Dark beloved, colour my veil). This sadhu had a dark complexion. With this in mind he said, "The colour of my body is already fast, but bless me so that my heart becomes saffron."
"The colour of the body may be anything; it does not matter. What matters is devotion in the heart." Swamishri explained the greatness of inner devotion.

Doing darshan, Swamishri came into the rupchoki above the mandir. A crowd of sadhus had gathered here, some who had come from abroad and some from abroad staying here at the training centre. They all said, "To become sadhus, learn saintliness and give up our bad natures."
Swamishri said, "Give up what?"
One sadhu said, "Our natures."
"Do you have them?" Swamishri asked.
That sadhu said, "Please be gracious."
Swamishri said, "Grace has already been given. How much more should I give? I made you a sadhu."
Saying this, as he passed by, he said, "Everyone's natures will go."

Today thousands of devotees had gathered for the diksha ceremony. To attend, some volunteers set out from Ahmedabad early in the morning. Five volunteers of the Hirawadi area, co director Karsanbhai I. Patel, Nilkanthbhai D. Thumar, Ambarishbhai Nanjibhai Patel, Mukeshbhai Vasani and others, were coming to Sarangpur early in the morning when their car collided with a truck near Dhandhuka, and the four volunteers passed away on the spot. The fifth volunteer, Ghanshyambhai Thumar, was badly injured. Swamishri received this news while the diksha ceremony was going on, so he had the sadhus make all the arrangements.

Even at such a divine and extraordinary occasion, Swamishri did not fail to pay tribute to them in his blessings. During his blessings Swamishri said, "Today something has happened that pains us. Devotees were coming here by car, and near Dhandhuka there was an accident and four brothers left their bodies. They were coming here; they were directors. It has happened by Maharaj's wish. God is the doer; whether to keep or end a life is all God's wish. If we have that knowledge, there is no wailing. What God has done is surely good. So for this let us do a dhun today. So that their souls find peace, God keeps them happy, and there is peace in their families too, let us do a little dhun." Saying this, Swamishri himself began the dhun 'Swaminarayan... Swaminarayan...'. For about five minutes Swamishri himself led the dhun.
On Wednesday 10 March 2010, over 4,000 devotees gathered to witness the auspicious Diksha Mahotsav in the presence of Pramukh Swami Maharaj in Sarangpur.

The initial Vedic Mahapuja rituals for the Diksha Mahotsav were performed by Mahant Swami, the initiates and their parents. Thereafter, Swamishri performed the concluding rituals and gave the guru-mantra to all the youths.
Swamishri initiated 21 youths, who had completed their initial training period, into the parshad-order and ordained 21 parshads into the sadhu-order.

Blessing the assembly, Swamishri said, “Diksha is to surrender totally to God. The youths are enthusiastic that they want to serve at the feet of God. Some parents have permitted their only sons. It is difficult (for parents) to do this. It is not an ordinary thing, but the parents have total faith that God will look after them. Shriji Maharaj will grant them happiness, peace, and physical, mental and financial well-being.

ds.t: Asking for the ability to prepare
w: After darshan in the mandir, Mahant Swami Maharaj came down to the podium. A student prayed, "Please bless us that we can prepare as well as possible."
Pleased by the words of the boy's prayer, Swamishri said, "He asked that we may be able to prepare, not just for blessings."
"I took a step, and you came to meet me, O Lord." Swamishri explains: you make the effort, and our blessings will shower upon you of their own accord.
